15-1.title: The Roman Republic
15-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE ROMAN REPUBLIC

Rome began on the Italian peninsula and grew into a powerful state. Importantly, Rome started as a REPUBLIC. A republic is a government in which citizens ELECT leaders to make decisions for them, instead of being ruled by a king. (Rome had once had kings, but Romans overthrew them and created the Republic.)

In the Roman Republic, citizens elected leaders, including powerful officials. The most important leaders were the SENATORS, who served in the Senate and helped run the government and make laws. To stop any one person from gaining too much power, Rome created a system with a SEPARATION OF POWERS — power was divided among different leaders and groups. Rome also believed in the RULE OF LAW, meaning everyone had to follow the law. Rome's early laws were written down in the Twelve Tables.

These ideas — electing leaders, separating powers, and the rule of law — later INFLUENCED many governments, including the UNITED STATES. Roman citizens were also expected to take part in government, a responsibility called CIVIC DUTY. Remember: a republic = citizens elect their leaders (Rome's early government).

questions.question: Rome's early government was a what?
questions.explanation: Rome began as a republic.

questions.question: What is a republic?

choices.B: A government ruled by one all-powerful king
choices.D: A government where citizens elect their leaders

questions.question: What were Rome's important elected leaders called?

questions.question: Why did Rome use a 'separation of powers'?

choices.A: To give one king all power
choices.B: To stop any one person from gaining too much power

questions.explanation: Separation of powers prevented one person from controlling everything.

questions.question: The Roman idea that everyone must follow the law is called the what?
questions.explanation: The rule of law means everyone must obey the law.

questions.question: Which later country was influenced by Roman ideas of government?
questions.explanation: Roman ideas influenced the United States government.

questions.question: The duty of Roman citizens to take part in government was called what?
questions.explanation: Taking part in government is called civic duty.

questions.question: How was a republic DIFFERENT from rule by a king?

choices.B: Citizens elected their leaders instead of obeying one king

questions.explanation: A republic lets citizens elect leaders, unlike a single king's rule.

questions.question: Rome's earliest written laws were known as the what?
questions.explanation: Rome's early laws were the Twelve Tables.

questions.question: Which list correctly names Roman ideas that influenced later governments?

choices.A: Elected leaders, separation of powers, rule of law

questions.explanation: Elected leaders, separation of powers, and rule of law are Roman influences.

15-2.title: The Punic Wars and Roman Expansion
15-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE PUNIC WARS AND ROMAN EXPANSION

As Rome grew stronger, it came into conflict with another powerful trading city, CARTHAGE, located in North Africa. Rome and Carthage fought three long, brutal wars called the PUNIC WARS over control of the Mediterranean Sea and its trade.

The Punic Wars produced one of history's most famous generals: HANNIBAL of Carthage. In a daring move, Hannibal marched his army — including WAR ELEPHANTS — over the snowy Alps mountains to attack Rome from the north. He won several battles and nearly defeated Rome.

In the end, however, ROME WON all three Punic Wars. Rome eventually destroyed the city of Carthage completely. These victories were a huge turning point: they made Rome the MASTER of the Mediterranean, giving it control of valuable land, trade, and resources across the region. Winning the Punic Wars set the stage for Rome to grow from a regional power into a mighty empire that would dominate the ancient Mediterranean world. Remember: Punic Wars = Rome vs. Carthage; Hannibal's elephants; Rome won.

questions.question: Who won the Punic Wars?
questions.explanation: Rome won all three Punic Wars.

questions.question: What were the Punic Wars mostly fought over?

choices.B: Control of the Mediterranean and its trade

questions.explanation: The wars were over control of the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Over which mountains did Hannibal march his army and elephants?

questions.question: What finally happened to the city of Carthage?

choices.A: It became the capital of Rome

questions.explanation: Rome eventually destroyed Carthage.

questions.question: Why were the Punic Wars a major turning point for Rome?

choices.D: They made Rome the master of the Mediterranean

15-3.title: From Republic to Empire
15-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS — FROM REPUBLIC TO EMPIRE

As Rome grew huge and powerful, its REPUBLIC began to struggle. There were problems like fighting between rich and poor, growing armies loyal to their generals, and political violence. In this troubled time, a brilliant general named JULIUS CAESAR rose to power and took control of Rome, ruling almost like a king. Many senators feared he had too much power, so a group of them ASSASSINATED (killed) Caesar in 44 BC.

Caesar's death led to more civil war. In the end, Caesar's adopted heir, OCTAVIAN, defeated his rivals and took power. He took the name AUGUSTUS and became the FIRST EMPEROR of Rome. This change marked the end of the Roman Republic and the beginning of the ROMAN EMPIRE.

Under Augustus, Rome entered a long period of PEACE and stability called the PAX ROMANA, meaning 'Roman Peace,' which lasted about 200 years. The most important change was that POWER shifted from elected leaders (the Republic) to ONE powerful emperor (the Empire). Remember: Republic = elected leaders; Empire = ruled by an emperor. Augustus was Rome's first emperor.

questions.question: Which Roman general took control of Rome before being assassinated?
questions.explanation: Julius Caesar seized power and was then assassinated.

questions.question: Who became the FIRST emperor of Rome?
questions.explanation: Augustus (Octavian) became Rome's first emperor.

questions.question: What is the Pax Romana?

choices.C: A long period of Roman peace

questions.explanation: The Pax Romana was a long period of Roman peace.

questions.question: What does 'Pax Romana' mean?
questions.explanation: Pax Romana means 'Roman Peace.'

questions.question: What was the BIGGEST change as Rome went from Republic to Empire?

choices.C: Power shifted from elected leaders to one emperor
choices.D: Rome had no leader at all

questions.explanation: Power moved from elected leaders to a single emperor.

questions.question: What happened to Julius Caesar?

choices.B: He died of old age peacefully

questions.explanation: Senators assassinated Julius Caesar.

questions.question: About how long did the Pax Romana last?
questions.explanation: The Pax Romana lasted roughly 200 years.

questions.question: Why did senators fear Julius Caesar?

choices.A: He was too weak to rule
choices.B: They thought he had gained too much power

questions.explanation: Senators feared Caesar had become too powerful.

questions.question: What was the name Octavian took when he became emperor?
questions.explanation: Octavian took the name Augustus.

questions.question: How is the Roman Empire DIFFERENT from the Roman Republic?

choices.A: The Empire was ruled by an emperor; the Republic elected its leaders

questions.explanation: The Empire had one emperor; the Republic elected leaders.
